correctness.rationale: At every fixed integer \(n\ge3\) and \(\alpha>0\), boundedness is equivalent to all cyclic Dirichlet gaps <1/2, the polygon area equals its semiperimeter and the sum of tangent half-gap lengths. Beta marginal density \(f(1/2)=2^{2-n\alpha}/\mathrm{B}(\alpha,(n-1)\alpha)\) is finite positive. A single gap at 1/2-O(1/t) gives leading f(1/2)/(pi t) probability with conditional boundedness loss O(t^(-1-(n-2)alpha)); pairs of large gaps have that same higher-order corner bound. An exact max/sum squeeze yields n f(1/2)/(pi t); dividing by positive boundedness probability gives c. Layer-cake proves all real moments \(q<1\) and divergence \(q\ge1\). Shoelace geometry, beta CDF edge, and finite numerical tails independently checked using the bundled verify.py. No numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The standard random circumscribed-circle polygon has a natural but previously unquantified large-area tail. The explicit coefficient for every fixed \(n\ge3\) and \(\alpha>0\), universal \(t^{-1}\) exponent, exact all-real-moment cutoff, and one-nearly-semicircular-gap mechanism give structural information essential when using the area as an approximation statistic. In particular, a normal approximation in the \(n\to\infty\) regime need not imply finite means at any finite n. This is mathematically motivated rather than a narrow arbitrary parameter sample.
